NERF Thunderhawk Nerf AccuStrike Mega Toy Blaster - Longest Nerf Blaster - 10 Official AccuStrike Nerf Mega Darts, 10-Dart Clip, Bipod My boys(5, 7, and 10) love Nerf guns. It's been a main request for birthdays and Christmas over the past year. For my 10 year old's last birthday, he requested a Nerf war. It was beyond fun to see the adults(of all ages) getting in on the fun right alongside the children. This one has a cool factor, since it's the longest Nerf gun at the moment and it truly is Mega. You can slide the barrel out to make it longer and slide it back in to make it shorter. It also has a bipod.

On the negative side, it takes up a great deal of room. It's a bit of a pain with its size. It's also so big that it's hard for my boys to use. I tried to use it and it's even awkward for me. I'd recommend this gun more for teens and adults. The only way my boys are really able to use it is with the bipod. It is a bit easier in the shorter length, but it's still heavy and awkward.

It also takes larger bullets than the average Nerf gun. It's a pain to have to worry about buying 2 separate kinds of bullets. All the rest of what we have take the same ones, and it makes things simpler. This gun comes with 10, but my boys lose darts constantly. Many times we discover where they were after the lawnmower turns them to confetti. Prepare for an extra investment if you don't already have other Mega guns.

Overall, if you don't mind buying the bigger bullets that go with this one and you or your child can handle the size, it's a pretty cool gun. My boys have had a hard time overly enjoying it, though, even if they do find it cool.
text_fidelity_b: NERF Thunderhawk Nerf AccuStrike Mega Toy Blaster - Longest Nerf Blaster - 10 Official AccuStrike Nerf Mega Darts, 10-Dart Clip, Bipod

text_fidelity_a:
Treasure X King's Gold Treasure Tomb We have had a few other Treasure X sets in the past and my son really enjoyed them, with the sets keeping him busy for hours at a time carving and opening little slime filled packages with interesting toys inside. He has a castle "dollhouse" that he uses a lot of these toys in to create stories.

This treasure tomb was completely different in the sense that we work carving the toys out of chunks of sand this time, rather discovering each element and kind of figuring out everything as a puzzle.

The one criticism I have is that while I would've loved to have set this down and let my son just figure it out, the texture of a few of the things that you were supposed to just pick apart and peel away were not necessarily obvious that they were disposable elements of the toy, so the instruction manual was necessary, and because the instruction manual was not made big and pictorial, I had to sit there while they figured the whole thing out. My six-year-old figured out and understood most of it, but again, the parts that were not obvious that he was allowed to just tear into them really did need my reading the instructions and giving encouragement.

Aside from that minor quibble, this thing kept both my six-year-old and my three and half-year-old busy for a really long time. Hours. I sat them outside on the patio with a big pan to hold any messy elements, and they carved and drove swords into holes and put the keys in and popped everything out and overall had a ridiculously fun time.

The weird textural blue rock like slime in two of the tombs was particularly compelling to my son, who played with this stuff for about 45 minutes. I would've appreciated if the two tombs had had different types of slime or even just different colors, but my son had no such complaint and played for a long time.

While the tomb itself has not continued to hold their interest after about a week of play, some of the parts have been incorporated into frequent play with their castle dollhouse, and so overall even though part of it feels somewhat disposable, the other parts of it feel really fun for incorporating into our normal imaginative play.

This would make a fantastic birthday gift, because it is extremely flashy, tons of fun, lots of excited commentary and wowed children, and then lots of little toys that feel very fun and abundant.

Would I buy a set like this again? Very possibly, for a holiday or other occasion that I really want to feel super special and fancy. If there was a holiday where we were unable to have family and friends visit us or something like that, this set would bridge the gap to make the day feel sparkly and exciting for the kids.
text_fidelity_b: Treasure X King's Gold Treasure Tomb

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats This is seriously one of the cutest games ever! I love the variety within it, too.

First of all, the anteaters themselves are very well made! You get two of them. Sometimes you get "masks" and they're pretty crappy, but these are quality. To wear these, there's two felt-like straps that will fit along the back of a child's head, along with velcro piece at the end of one strap. This means it will fit pretty much any child's head, because you can tighten or loosen as much of the strap as you want. There's another piece of velcro attached to the underside of the anteater's snout. This is what picks up the felt-like ants. Super, super cute!

Within this set is also the instructions, of course, along with a timer and a set of cards. These cards are similar to the cards within most matching games out there. We have several of them. They are small, square, and thick. One side of each of them simply shows an anteater at a picnic. The other side either shows various types of food for a matching game(This is also great for speech development!), or one or the other side of a colorful ant. This is also for matching, and a great way for the youngest players to learn colors. There are also a few "tummy ache" cards, which shows a sick anteater. A player will lose cards they've matched when this card comes into play.

You can really mix and match the various games in any way you want, especially depending on the ages involved. You can simply play "hide and seek" with the ants, or allow a player to find an ant once they find a match within the cards, or find the color of the ant they've matched together. You can add the timer for the older players or just to add a bit more challenge, if desired. You can also simply play a matching game with the cards for a quieter game. There are many possibilities for playing this game, so I imagine it will take longer to get "old" for most little ones.

Overall, this is a wonderful game, and one of the most fun ones we've had the pleasure of playing!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats

My style is more along the lines of giving them art supplies and letting them create what they want, and honestly, that's what I'll always prefer for them. They really enjoy projects that have a somewhat defined end result sometimes, though, and so it's kits like this that come to my rescue. I could turn my children loose with everything and see what they come up with, but I prefer separating each project(at least for the most part), so that my children can choose which one they want to do, and not worry about running out of supplies before all the project are finished. Between my 3 children, I'll get 5 rainy days out of this box, with one extra. (I can't beat that!) ;) Plus, the included finger crayons can be used after all the projects are finished.

Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up Kinetic sand is a fun activity for young kids, like regular sand it has tendency to get all over the place if not contained in a tray or plastic dish but it is easy to clean up and unlike play-doh and other similar modeling toys it doesn't ever dry out. This bake shop set comes with a roller and variety of stamps and molds to make cookies and cupcakes which are all nice quality. I especially like that the molds can fit within the roller for easy storage.

The only downside to this set is that kinetic sand is not really ideal for molding since it has a tendency to flow and collapse if not packed very tightly. Our 5 year old was trying to reproduce some of the cupcake designs shown on the box and was getting frustrated because the sand kept falling apart when she added the icing on top of the cupcake base. I tried to do it myself and was able to reproduce the design but it required packing the sand very tightly and then being very delicate when removing from the molds..

We like kinetic sand, and we like the molds that come with this set but we will probably use them primarily with play-doh instead of kinetic sand because these small molds are kind of difficult for kids to use with kinetic sand. We have some other larger ice cream molds that we have used with kinetic sand in the past, they are easier to use because they are smoother and release the sand without requiring such a delicate touch to prevent it crumbling.
text_fidelity_b: Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up

LEGO City Race Boat Transporter 60254 Race Boat Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (238 Pieces) This LEGO CITY RACE BOAT TRANSPORTER BUILDING SET ((60254) New 2020, 238 Pieces) is fairly easy to build--the difficulty is what I’d call “normal” for a City-themed set. City sets are among my favorites, because they include fire trucks, police stations, buses, trains, beachgoer minifigs, space stations, and all the rest of the things that a bustling city (or the airspace above it) needs. This particular set is aimed at ages 5 and up.

The set contains all the pieces required to build three separate items: a semi-trailer truck (for towing the race boat), a trailer for hauling the race boat, and a race boat. (You can use the truck’s trailer hitch to tow other things that you build, of course.)

The “Xtreme” graphics are NOT printed on the pieces, but are applied with stickers. (I hate stickers, too.) Applying stickers is made easier if you first stick a corner to something long and thin (e.g., a spudger or a plastic knife) so that you can better control the placement on the element. A good thing about LEGO stickers is that they can be removed and replaced (like Post-Its) if you get them misaligned.

The LEGO elements are compatible with other City sets and with all regular LEGO sets (but not with DUPLO sets, which have extra-large pieces for very young builders). The Race Boat Transporter set is another fine addition to the extensive collection of City sets.

This is important so students understand that even whole numbers can be written in fraction form for when they move into mixed numbers and further, into making whole numbers into fractions to solve more complicated arithmetic.

Not a deal breaker though! Easy enough just to write it on there with a sharpie. Would definitely purchase again.

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball I'm someone who will cheat at something if I can. Like when I was was a kid, and I played [[ASIN:B00000IWCT Monopoly]] with my little brothers, I would steal money from the bank, just because I could.

Each piece of this puzzle has a number on the back of it, and the numbers tell you which pieces fit together. So, it's much easier to flip over all of the pieces of the puzzle, and put it together upside down, that by putting the puzzle together by the picture. And it's much easier by a lot. I think that everyone who does this puzzle will eventually get frustrated, and resort to doing the puzzle upside down, which I consider 'cheating.'

It's very solid, and very strong, when you put it together. The pieces are made of sturdy plastic, not cardboard, like other puzzles. Also the pieces seem like they're cast, or molded, and not cut. That's why the globe surface ends up smooth. But, because all of the pieces were manufactured separately, instead as a whole puzzle, then the picture doesn't always match up from piece to piece.

It comes with a cheap stand, but it looks pretty nice when it's assembled and displayed. I hid a few coins in the middle of it, so it rattles when you move it. It's got lot of area in the middle for a small sphere, so it could double as a secret safe.

Pros:
+Very sturdy, especially when the sphere is completed
+Nice picture, with a bunch of cool zodiac symbols
+High quality

Cons:
-Has numbers on the back of each piece of the puzzle, so it's super simple to assemble
-Plastic, so it doesn't feel like a real puzzle
-The picture doesn't always line up from piece to piece
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

text_fidelity_a:
Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories The Schleich barn is made of wood and is of extremely high quality except for a problem with the clips and pieces of wood that hold the barn roof together.

The barn opens into two separate unattached halves that slide together at right angles like a puzzle. There are latches on either short side of the barn that can be unlatched to display each half. The barn can be left open or closed. When closed it is easy to carry. A cow, chicken, donkey, lamb, hay bale, basket, red and green vegetables, and a pitch fork and broom are the accessories included. The barn doors on the long side of the barn open in both front and back. The color is vibrant and the farm animals are very realistic.

The only negative I found is that the entire barn is held together with clips that come apart. The clips are not its strongest point. The four clips on either side of the barn roof on mine would not hold up the roof and the boards keep falling off. I tried for over 30 minutes to get two of the clips seated correctly but neither side would snap in place. My boyfriend also looked at this barn and he could not get the clips to seat firmly in place either. He did say, however, that this is a well-made toy. According to the side of the box below the Germany label, it says this is made in Slovakia.

The clips and vegetable pieces that come with the barn can present a choking hazard to a small child. If the child is of that age where items are frequently "tasted," then I recommend adult supervision while the child is playing with this barn. The box indicates that this is not for children under 3 years of age and does state that the small parts present a choking hazard. This is typical of many toys with small parts, however.

Other than this, I got this for my friend's son to play with and he's going to love it. However, he'll have to play with the two roof slats off since they will fall off in its current condition. If the unit I received did not have this problem, I would have rated this 5 stars. Since mine does have this problem, I'm rating it 3. Had I purchased this unit and not received it for review, I would have returned it for a replacement. text_fidelity_a:
The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games I'm a wolf lover as well as a game nerd and couldn't pass this one up! It is absolutely beautiful out of the box. I'm impressed they kept it to a $50 price point with the level of detail here, I've seen similar games priced closer to $80!

I haven't had a chance to play yet because I need to get folks together but I did watch a video playthrough about the rules after reading the guide so that I'd be prepared. They are complex but once I watched the video it made a lot more sense. It's definitely tactic-heavy in that you need to change strategy based on what your opponent is doing or what phase of the moon it is on. I love many of the creative points in the design, and I love a game with a very clear endpoint because I hate games that go on forever! 75 minutes is perfect for a game night.

I especially love the design of the wolf cards. They are extremely clear where the tiles and meeples go etc. It's not only attractive but it also includes reminder text which is really helpful for absent-minded players like myself. I love how the rules for your items level up as you get more pieces on the board.

My favorite part about games like this is that it's possible to lose a battle here and there and not feel discouraged halfway through. Since a lot of scoring can happen later, it keeps players invested until the end. This generation of games is so different from the ones before!

My only complaint is that with a game like this it is so easy to lose a meeple because they are so small and so many. This can make it hard to trust strangers with at board-game meetups.
text_fidelity_b: The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games

text_fidelity_a:
Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626 I wear a silicone ring and truly like it. Perhaps prefer it because I don't worry about it like I do gold or silver, nor do I tend to hook it (sometimes painfully) on things. I recently noticed the Enso Rings Collections and liked much of what I saw, so when I spotted this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection available I grabbed it. In this case, for my wife. I am a Disney fan as well, but Stitch is one of her favorites, and honestly, I was not a big fan of the red - I prefer blue or black in silicone and the traditional silvers and golds. So... how would we like this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection?

1. It arrived in a nice little packaging making great for protecting the ring, displaying the ring, and a nice presentation for gifting. Great all around.

2. Sizing. Honestly, this was the hardest part. Sizing your finger is never the easiest of tasks as we have discovered. But in this case they wanted the inside of a ring rather than your finger. We have a flexible, cloth type measuring tape, but still, trying to get that in there and with the metal end and lined up and staying in place as you pull it out.. not fun. They do have their sizes to the rounded whole - I feel like I remember others with in between sizes, which would make this harder. In the end we went with the one we got consistently and hoped. Turned out great - fits my wife's middle finger as she wanted and my ring finger.

3. The red is actually pretty cool. Again, not my favorite on the spectrum of ring colors, but my wife loves it and I like it. And for the Lilo and Stitch option, it works. There is a sparkle to it - both nice and not overwhelming.

4. The in-print on the ring feels "subtle," but present; something you can see, but at a glance it's more like a light-shadow affect. Upon closer examination you spot the little Lilo (not a fave character for either of us), but the Stitch rocks. And the little flower brings out the Polynesian flavor, while giving the whole thing a sweet nod to Disney. For a Disney fan, it's a great find.

5. This is my wife's first silicone, but like me, she's liking it. It is comfortable, easy to wear, does not catch on things in the same way (but all rings do catch), and it has that silicone flexibility that makes wearing it more comfortable in many situations.

6. I have found in wearing silicone I have to be more careful when washing my hands. Soap can build up behind and/or keep up the wetness between ring and finger, and can come off easier when drying. I warned her and sure enough, same thing. So do be careful. Additionally, she finds there is a (slight) risk of stuff like soap building up in the little grooves. No worries, what little she thinks she saw (it's tiny) washed out easily. And so far, after two weeks, it continues to look like new.

In the end she really likes this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection and is so happy to have this Stitch ring. I've seen a few others on their pages I'd consider, so yes, we'd get another Enso ring. Always fun to wear an ode to something that makes you smile.
text_fidelity_b: Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626

text_fidelity_a:
Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game The predecessor to this game, Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective, is my all-time favorite game, and holds a high place on my game shelf despite being a “one and done” experience. Does this new iteration hold up to the high standard the previous game established?

To start with, the production value on this new version is heads and shoulders above the 2013 edition of SHCD that I own. The paper is printed on much nicer stock, the box is thicker and better designed to hold the contents, and the instruction manual in particular shows a great attention to detail that the previous edition lacked. I particularly like that in this edition, the solutions to each case are printed upside down in the back of the box, and that the solutions are encased in an envelope secured to each case book to prevent spoiling any aspects of the story with erroneous page turns.

Like the previous game, this “board game” is much more of a “choose your own adventure” story for you and your friends to solve. Each case is represented by a book, in which you’re given an introductory story, and then allowed free reign to investigate a variety of leads and allies to assist you in gathering information about whodunit. Once you think you know what’s happening, turn to the questions and find out what happened in this story – don’t worry, there are significant explanations and story to give closure to each case.

This is a stand-alone game, meaning that if you haven’t already played the original SHCD, you can purchase this with no strings attached. I don’t think I would recommend that for new players, however.

Jack the Ripper and the West End Adventures are quite different from what you get in the original game. In the original, there were some threads of story that remained from one case to the next, but in the new version, four of the cases are designed to be played campaign-style in an effort to solve the Jack the Ripper murders.

I’m sure that there will be many people out there who love the Jack the Ripper campaign - a set of four cases that are thematically tied together that will allow you to hunt down Jack using a separate map and additional investigative helpers – but it really isn’t for me. First of all, the cases are quite a bit darker and less whimsical than your traditional Sherlock Holmes story and case, and are tied together only by the fact that they occur in the same area and time period. I think the original cases are too difficult to be played by, let’s say, a 10 year old, but the stories wouldn’t be inappropriate for them in terms of language and description. The Jack cases, on the other hand, would carry a definite R-rating – they’re well-researched historically, and include lots of graphic description and a few cuss words as well. If you know anything about the historical Jack cases, you’d probably know this going in, but if you’re used to the style of the original cases, know that this is a darker affair. Secondly, you absolutely cannot find Jack and get a satisfactory conclusion until the fourth case, which is a decent investment in time with little return for parts 1 - 3. Third, and this is the big reason I didn’t like it, is that the mini-mysteries you’re solving in parts 1, 2 and 3 are not mysteries at all, but historical backstory. The questions are answered directly by particular sources, so if you visit the right allies and pursue the right leads you will simply be given the correct answers to each piece without putting much of anything together outside of remembering what the leads gave you. This was a very different experience, with a different writing style, different thematic elements, and a wholly different style, and since I am such a fan of the tried-and-true SHCD formula, I did not enjoy it as much as others may.

The other six cases are all stand-alone cases, and are quite good, although in most cases, they’re quite a bit harder than the already difficult cases in the original box. Like that set, some are better than others, but I will admit that the overall quality of these cases is on-par with what came in the original box, but still harder. I don’t think this is the right place to start with the SHCD universe.

Therein lies the only real problem that I have with this SHCD set – that while packaged as a stand-alone, this game is put together in a way that strongly suggests that it’s a sequel. If you think of it in movie terms, sure, you can watch most sequels without seeing the original movies, but why would you, especially if you know going in that watching the original is going to improve your experience? The cases in this box are more difficult, and the Jack the Ripper set is an odd starting place.

Overall, this game comes very highly recommended to any fan of the original set of cases. If this game sounds like something you’d be interested in, get it, but be advised that I think that the original set of 10 cases are a superior starting place.

4.5/5
text_fidelity_b: Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game

The projector is difficult to position over the flashlight on my Galaxy S10 phone, unless I turn the phone over and look through the lens at the light. This burns an image into my retina, and is clearly not good for my eyes!

The projector clips onto the phone, and exerts moderate pressure on the screen. I don’t like this, because I worry about cracking the screen.

The projector works with the free “Moonlite” app (available from the App Store or Google Play). You will have to register for an account to use the app. After that, you must activate each set of story reels by entering an activation code--the code is on a small card packed in the box. You tap the “unlock” icon at the top left of the app, and enter the code.

Once you’ve activated the story reel set, you click on the story you want. The app will then display a story for you to read to your child. As you read each page, you advance the reel in the Moonlite projector, to get a new illustration for each page of the story.

The projector shows a focused illustration (focus is adjustable), as long as you are no more than a yard or so away from the surface you are projecting to. You cannot project the picture across a room, or for any great distance, because the phone’s flashlight isn’t bright enough to project for long distances.

The photos that accompany the stories in the Disney set are boring, as are the stories. Kids will no doubt love the Disney characters in the pictures (e.g., Mickey, Minnie, Donald, Goofy), but the story illustrations are repetitious. Also the detail in the illustrations gets lost because the projected images are fairly small.
text_fidelity_b: Moonlite Mini Projector with 5 Classic Winnie The Pooh Stories - A New Way to Read Stories Together - 5 Digital Stories with Light Projector - Winnie The Pooh Toys and Gifts for Kids Ages 1 and Up

Repos JUST01 Just One, Various There are a lot of "just one word clues" games out there, from Codenames and Decrypto to games like Funglish, Crosstalk or Word Slam, and this game is yet another to add to that group. I think, however, that it's my secnd favorite of the bunch, and if you need a Codenames Killer, this might be up your alley.

In this team game, one player is attempting to guess a word that the rest of their team knows. Each team member writes down one word only, then compares to see if any matches are detected. If they are, those cards are discarded, and the guesser is left with fewer clues. Therefore, the more obtuse clues you get, the more you'll have, but it can be more difficult to deduce the word than if you're given a few obvious clues.

What I like about this game is that it manages to be a louder than usual team game with secrets. In Codenames or Crosstalk, two previous iterations of the concept, games are fun, but often it's players staring at the board in silence. In this one, you still can't say much, but it does lend itself to quicker play, and it's easier to communicate more freely once you have your clues written since your work is done, and the stress of the round is over for the clue-givers. This is a hard game, and it's definitely a word game, but lends itself to being an excellent family gathering game.
text_fidelity_b: Repos JUST01 Just One, Various

There's tape everywhere, including a cover over the screen. The unit itself it held in with clips you have to turn, a twist-tie that holds the stylus as well as tape that blocks the cord that holds the stylus in place.
On top of that nightmare it says to erase the screen turn the unit over and shake it four times. I've had a horrible time trying to get the screen to erase. Sometimes the screen seems to erase in sections while it sits upright doing nothing. When it's working it's actually kind of fun. The stylus writes well thin and thick and the stampers are double sides and can leave stars, clouds, circle & crown plus the edges can be used to draw straight double lines a half inch apart on the screen. It's got some flaws but it can be a lot of fun to play with. I can't say it's a great toy, not with the hassles and problems it's given me plus, for some reason it takes two button batteries (it comes with them pre-installed but doesn't mention on average how long they'll last) that require a screwdriver and likely a trip to a specialty battery shop or some place that sells watch batteries as it doesn't say what size batteries it takes.

Testors Decal Paper, Clear, Pack of 6 (9201) I'm giving this product 4-stars partly because what was in the envelope was not what I ordered (white not clear), and because the sheets are small and there are only 6 of them for the price. Having found a work-around so I could use white substrate, I find this decal material relatively easy to use and can say the end result is quite suitable.

Here's what produced the best results:
1) Printed the images (inkjet Epson ET) and let them dry at least over night.
2) Sprayed them with one coat Krylon Crystal Clear Acrylic Coating, and let that dry for an hour or so. Acrylic clear coat is essential to getting a high quality finished result.
3) Applied a second coat of the Krylon and let is dry for about an hour.
4) Cut the images very close to remove as much of the white backing as possible.
5) Placed the decal in water with the backing side in the water. The edges curled up and I had to hold them flat for a few seconds to get the decals to lay flat in the water.
6) When the edges of the decal substrate (what the image is printed on) began to curl away from the backing sheet, I removed the backing sheet with the now loosened decal from the water and gently slid the decal off the backing sheet and onto my project surface.
7) Patted the decal gently with tissue to remove excess water from under and around the decal.
8) Set the project aside and allowed all moisture to dry. This assures the decal is set onto the piece.
9) Sprayed the project with two top coats of Krylon, with about two hours between spraying. This assures the decal is not easily scratched or marred.

What DID NOT WORK was floating the decal design side down in the water. This wets the Krylon coat too much and when you slide the decal off the backing and onto the project, some ink leeches out into the water and moist Krylon creating a slimy, grayish muck and tends to ruin the graphic.

I also searching for another brand that offers more and larger sheets for just a little more money.
text_fidelity_b: Testors Decal Paper, Clear, Pack of 6 (9201)

Legacy Deluxe Mancala Classic Game with Folding Wooden Game Board and Colored Glass Stones, Family Game for Ages 8 and up Chess has been my favorite board game since I was a child and I have collected chess sets as a hobby over the years. When I selected this one I expected it to be on par with typical portable wooden sets which are usually cheaply made. This one was a pleasant surprise in that it is a step up from most portable wooden sets I have seen and used.

This is a fairly straightforward set. The case is a clamshell design that folds open into the board. There are magnets in the rim of the underside of the board to hold it closed when the set is not in use, ands the manufacturer did a decent job of concealing the contacts (though they are visible if you look for them). The squares on the board are smooth and while the seams between the squares can be felt when you run your hand along the board, the seams are smooth and are less pronounced that what I have seen on some other boards.

The pieces are decently made though are nothing special. They are machine cut pieces and have been smoothed, sanded and varnished. They are weighted nicely and have felt on the bottom to avoid scratching the board. They’re a fairly average design but they look good and are very recognizable.

The main feature of this set is that it is larger than most fold-out boards I have seen and used. While this might not be the best for packing and portability, I really like the size. I am less likely to knock over pieces accidentally and I can see what’s going on a little better.

This is not just a chess set but includes wood chips for playing checkers as well. The chips are small and are nothing of note but they are sufficient.

I really like this chess set and will use it as my main travel set moving forward. I like the size of the board, the feel of the pieces and the overall quality. There are better sets out there but they cost more. There are less expensive sets too, and the chances of finding one that is of the same quality as this one for less is small.

Barbie Dream Closet Playset with 30+ Clothes and Accessories Including 5 Outfits, Plus Mirror, Desk and Rotating Rack The Barbie Dream Closet is indeed a very happy dream realized. There’s so much space to store all of the clothes and accessories, as well any additional clothing items you already own for Barbie. The mini hangers work great with the clothing rack, as there’s a bit of a grip to the hooks so the hangers stay in place, but are easy to put on and take off. The system is also super convenient to carry around due to its folded design, which latches in the front with a Barbie labeled lever, and the handle on top lets this go anywhere with ease. I do love that this set encourages all sorts of ways to be fun, adventurous, sporty, fancy, and smart with the closet decals, clothes and accessories (lab coat and shoes, laptop, fancy dress with jewelry and shoes, scuba gear, etc).

A few criticisms though…the nob on top to turn the clothing rack is a bit hard to spin, both in resistance and due to the short nob. I do wish it was a little bit looser and the nob was a little bit taller to make it easier to grab.
There are a few areas that fold in and out for storage, as well as shelves to place things, but I think it would have been nice for some sort of drawer system. The drawers would have been helpful for storing the mini bracelet, necklace, hair brush, sunglasses, etc to give them a good home when not in use. Using my imagination, it would have been extra fun if the full-length mirror had a battery operated set of mini Hollywood lights to add some flare. I think some extra touches like the drawers and mirror lights would make the price worth it. I think it’s just a tad on the expensive side for it lacking some details, although it's worth reiterating that the included pieces offer a lot of good play and imagination.

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer 4-In-1 Stroll 'N Trike, Red Radio Flyer Tricycle, Toddler Bike When I saw the opportunity to review this Radio Flyer four-in-one tricycle, I was eager to accept: My cousin and his wife, who live a couple doors down the street, have a three-year-old, and they have just learned that they are expecting another baby in June. So I knew that this toy would be used in all four of its "incarnations" at one point or another.

The toy arrived within three days, even though I did not request any special shipping status.

The directions for putting the tricycle together are excellent and detailed. They are entirely pictorial, with no words at all, which is a godsend for those of us who labor for hours trying to read badly translated written instructions. Laura (the mom) put the entire tricycle together with only minimal help from Brian (the dad). Brian did have to help with Instruction #13, and also with tightening screws and bolts here and there. I was delighted to hear that one does not need an engineering degree to put this toy together.

The tricycle went together very easily for the most part. The handlebars are the hardest part of the construction. Laura recommends that anyone putting this tricycle together pull up on the handlebars after attaching the bars and the clamp to be sure that the clamp has tightened properly. She pulled up on the handlebars at least four times and was able to remove them despite that clamp being on. You just have to tighten the clamp as much as possible.

This tricycle seems very durable, though I will add to this review after Brandon (the three-year-old) has used the toy more. The canopy is very nice, and the straps on the seat will be great for the new baby when he or she can use it (at nine months or so). The cupholder that surrounds the infant in the seat will be great for the baby as well. My only wish is that the tricycle had rubber tires instead of plastic tires. We live in a somewhat rural area with no sidewalks, and the plastic tires may not hold up as well as rubber tires. The push handle, to be used for infants, adjusts to the height of the adult pushing the tricycle, which is a wonderful feature.

Now to the acid test: Does the child like the toy? Brandon has been off this tricycle only to eat and sleep ever since it was put together. He even attempted to get on it several times while his mom was putting it together, saying, "I should try it!" With winter coming on he will probably use it only in the house at first, but Brian and Laura have a huge basement, and riding his tricycle there will give him hours of play time.

I highly recommend this tricycle, especially if your child or children are young enough to take advantage of it in all its formations. The product description says it can be used from nine months to five years, and that sounds about right.
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer 4-In-1 Stroll 'N Trike, Red Radio Flyer Tricycle, Toddler Bike

The gameplay is tremendous. My grandson loved the interactions and started asking many "how does that work" questions. We added ping pong and make-up balls to make things even more tremendous. Chloe, the cat, however, refused to ride in the truck.

This set will provide many hours of fun learning for any child.
